questions.question_text: At the same temperature, a solution of a monoprotic strong acid with pH 2 has approximately how many times the hydrogen-ion concentration of one with pH 4?
questions.explanation: Each pH unit represents a tenfold change in hydrogen-ion concentration; a two-unit difference is 10² = 100-fold.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly distinguishes a concentrated acid from a strong acid?
questions.option_a: Concentration describes amount per volume; strength concerns extent of ionisation
questions.option_b: Every concentrated acid is strong and every dilute acid is weak
questions.option_c: Strength is measured only by colour
questions.option_d: Concentration and strength always mean the same thing
questions.explanation: Concentration is the amount of solute in a given volume; acid strength refers to ionisation in solution. A strong acid can be dilute, and a weak acid can be concentrated.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: When preparing a dilute acid solution in the laboratory, why should concentrated acid be added slowly to water with stirring?
questions.option_a: Dilution releases heat, and adding acid gradually helps control heating and splashing
questions.option_b: Water must be added to acid to prevent any ionisation
questions.option_c: The procedure converts the acid into a base
questions.option_d: Acid and water react only below freezing
questions.explanation: Dilution of concentrated acids is strongly exothermic; adding acid to a larger amount of water reduces the risk of local overheating and splashes.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Aqueous hydrochloric acid conducts electricity, whereas dry hydrogen chloride gas does not show the same behaviour. The key reason is that
questions.option_a: mobile ions form when HCl dissolves in water
questions.option_b: dry HCl contains no hydrogen or chlorine atoms
questions.option_c: water removes all electrons from the circuit
questions.option_d: HCl becomes a metal only in solution
questions.explanation: HCl ionises in water to form mobile hydronium and chloride ions, which carry charge; dry molecular HCl lacks freely mobile ions.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A farmer finds that soil is excessively acidic. Which amendment is commonly used to raise its pH?
questions.explanation: Basic substances such as quicklime (CaO) or slaked lime (Ca(OH)₂) can neutralise acidic soil; the amount should be based on soil testing.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Turmeric paper is dipped into an alkaline cleaning solution. Which colour change is expected?
questions.option_a: It changes from yellow to reddish-brown
questions.option_b: It changes from blue to red
questions.option_c: It becomes colourless in every case
questions.option_d: It turns black because of carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Turmeric is a natural indicator that turns reddish-brown in basic conditions; it remains yellow in acidic or neutral conditions.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A student adds excess sodium hydroxide to an aqueous copper(II) sulphate sample. Which visible product is expected?
questions.option_a: A blue precipitate of copper(II) hydroxide
questions.option_d: A red precipitate of copper metal
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ reacts with hydroxide ions to form insoluble blue Cu(OH)₂; this is a precipitation reaction, not simply indicator colour change.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Acid rain can accelerate the weathering of marble monuments. Which constituent of marble is attacked by acidic water?
questions.explanation: Marble is largely calcium carbonate, which reacts with acids and can be dissolved or eroded by acidic deposition.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which gases are major precursors of acid rain in the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides can form sulphuric and nitric acids through atmospheric reactions with water and oxidants.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A carbonate rock sample reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid and releases a gas that turns limewater milky. The gas is
questions.explanation: Carbonates react with acids to release CO₂, which forms insoluble calcium carbonate when passed through limewater.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A gas is passed through limewater; it first turns milky, but prolonged excess gas can clear the milkiness. Which sequence explains this?
questions.option_a: CaCO₃ precipitate forms, then soluble calcium hydrogen carbonate forms
questions.option_c: Oxygen forms a blue complex, then a red gas
questions.explanation: CO₂ first produces insoluble CaCO₃; excess CO₂ and water can convert it to soluble calcium hydrogen carbonate.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A metal carbonate reacts with an acid. Besides a salt and water, which product is released?
questions.explanation: Acid–carbonate reactions produce a salt, water and carbon dioxide gas.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: During electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride (brine), which gas is produced at the anode in the chlor-alkali process?
questions.explanation: Chloride ions are oxidised at the anode to chlorine; hydrogen forms at the cathode and sodium hydroxide remains in solution.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In the chlor-alkali process, hydrogen is released at the cathode because
questions.option_c: sodium metal oxidises there to hydrogen
questions.option_d: oxygen is reduced to carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: At the cathode, water gains electrons to form hydrogen gas and hydroxide ions; chloride is oxidised at the anode.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Heating sodium hydrogen carbonate releases carbon dioxide. Why is this salt useful in baking?
questions.option_a: The gas helps dough rise by forming bubbles
questions.option_b: It permanently removes all water from flour
questions.option_c: It converts starch directly into protein
questions.option_d: It prevents any gas formation in an oven
questions.explanation: On heating, sodium hydrogen carbonate releases CO₂; gas bubbles expand and help make baked products porous.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Tooth enamel is vulnerable when plaque acids lower mouth pH below about 5.5. What is the immediate chemical risk?
questions.option_d: Production of oxygen bubbles in teeth
questions.explanation: Acidic conditions promote dissolution of hydroxyapatite mineral in enamel; fluoride and saliva help protect or remineralise it.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A household uses washing soda to soften hard water. Which substance is washing soda?
questions.explanation: Washing soda is Na₂CO₃·10H₂O; carbonate ions can remove hardness-causing calcium and magnesium ions by precipitation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why is Plaster of Paris used to make a rigid cast around a fracture?
questions.option_a: It sets into a hard mass after taking up water
questions.option_c: It releases oxygen that welds bone
questions.option_d: It remains a liquid at room temperature
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris rehydrates and hardens, allowing a supportive mould or cast to immobilise a fracture.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why does Plaster of Paris harden after water is added?
questions.option_a: It rehydrates to form interlocking gypsum crystals
questions.option_c: It loses all sulphate ions as gas
questions.option_d: It undergoes electrolysis at room temperature
questions.explanation: Calcium sulphate hemihydrate takes up water and sets as calcium sulphate dihydrate (gypsum), producing a hard mass.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Blue crystals of hydrated copper sulphate become white on strong heating. What has chiefly been removed?
questions.explanation: Heating CuSO₄·5H₂O removes its water of crystallisation, leaving white anhydrous CuSO₄; water can restore the blue hydrate.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A hydrated salt crystal loses water on exposure to dry air and becomes powdery. This process is called
questions.explanation: Efflorescence is loss of water of crystallisation from a hydrated salt on exposure to air.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: For an ideal dilute aqueous solution at about 25 °C with pH 3, the hydrogen-ion concentration is approximately
questions.explanation: By definition pH = −log₁₀[H⁺], so pH 3 corresponds to approximately 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ under the stated approximation.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Equal volumes of a strong acid and strong base are mixed. Which information is needed before concluding that the final mixture is neutral?
questions.option_c: The names of the laboratory workers
questions.option_d: The boiling point of the glassware
questions.explanation: Neutrality depends on stoichiometric amounts of acid and base (and conditions); equal volumes alone do not guarantee equal reacting equivalents.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A sample of hydrated copper sulphate is gently heated and then a few drops of water are added. Which sequence is expected?
questions.option_a: Blue crystals become white, then blue returns
questions.option_b: White crystals become red, then black
questions.option_c: Green crystals become yellow, then remain yellow
questions.option_d: No colour change because hydration water is chemically impossible
questions.explanation: Heating can remove water of crystallisation from blue CuSO₄·5H₂O to leave white anhydrous CuSO₄; water restores the blue hydrate.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Aqueous sodium carbonate solution is alkaline mainly because carbonate ions
questions.option_a: react with water to produce some hydroxide ions
questions.option_c: are identical to sodium metal atoms
questions.option_d: remove every water molecule from solution
questions.explanation: Carbonate ions undergo hydrolysis in water, producing hydroxide ions and making the solution basic.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which formula is associated with bleaching powder as represented in standard school chemistry?
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is commonly represented as calcium oxychloride, CaOCl₂, in school-level chemistry.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Methyl orange is added to an alkaline solution. Which colour is expected?
questions.explanation: Methyl orange is yellow in alkaline solution and red in acidic solution; its transition range lies on the acidic side.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which acid is commonly present as the electrolyte in a lead-acid storage battery?
questions.explanation: A lead-acid battery uses sulphuric acid as its electrolyte.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT chemistry references, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A dilute acid reacts with magnesium ribbon, releasing a gas. Which test best identifies the gas?
questions.option_a: A lighted splint gives a characteristic pop
questions.explanation: Many metals above hydrogen react with dilute acids to release hydrogen, which burns with a characteristic pop when tested carefully.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which salt is used in standard school chemistry examples as a source of chlorine-based bleaching and disinfecting action?
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder is commonly represented as calcium oxychloride and releases available chlorine in suitable conditions.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Class X Science, Acids, Bases and Salts, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
